crossTeamComparison.summary: Major shift this week. All three teams scored in B range (83.75-85). VitalHire and Team Y both produced their strongest submissions of the project. Team X remains strong but format issues (three separate PDFs, 'I think' in narrative) cost them. Trigger conditions and ownership clarity are the differentiating strengths this week. Sunset provisions are the universal weak point -- Team X excepted.

ownership.note: VitalHire's CHRO shutdown authority with org chart is the best ownership structure produced. Team Y used actual Lakeside HR roster roles (Lindsey's catch). Team X has clear chain but internal contradiction between worksheet and narrative on shutdown authority.

monitoring.note: Team X's Tyler Craig produced the strongest monitoring section of the semester. Six metrics with frequency, role, and defined normal with bounds. VitalHire has breadth (9 metrics, some duplicated). Team Y has five metrics with mixed specificity.

triggers.note: VitalHire's graduated adverse impact response (1 month → review, 2 → pause, 3 → shutdown) is the cleanest trigger architecture. Team Y matches with slightly different thresholds. Both include EEOC complaint as immediate shutdown. Team X has strong specifics (four-fifths, 14:1 ratio) but one non-threshold trigger.

vendor_req.note: Team X and Team Y both have specific SLAs with graduated consequences. Team Y adds termination obligations (data access, transition support, three-breach clause). VitalHire's 10-day incident reporting is slower than the others.

sunset.note: Team X cross-references WK11 and WK12 with numbered conditions and thresholds. VitalHire has 6-month timeline with specific metrics (0.80, 15%). Team Y wrote 'Some conditions' with vague bullets and zero thresholds -- the only major failure in an otherwise strong submission.

budget.note: Team Y and VitalHire both explicitly address budget with role mapping. Team X mentions staying within budget but doesn't map costs and left the budget checkbox unchecked.

prof_format.note: Team Y's Lindsey converted Google Doc to Word with headers, color, figure captions. Team X submitted three separate PDFs with 'I think' in paragraph 2. VitalHire has duplicate rows and section attribution visible in headers.
